gen-dafont-origami-gf-sulphur-point: Brushy, single-stroke and unusual up top. Sulphur Point sits underneath with open gaps in its letters and a bulky lowercase, so the pair feels sturdy, marker-drawn and quietly modern.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-tiktok-sans: Origami draws every stroke like a sign-painter's brush, one width all the way around, with lowercase as dense as poured lead. And TikTok Sans answers with an x-height rising nearly to cap height, which makes the body feel modern and open.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-ubuntu-sans: Ubuntu Sans brings lowercase eyes as big as washers and tubular strokes like bent copper pipe. Ubuntu Sans against Origami's brushy, lead-heavy heading makes a pair that feels contemporary and a bit unexpected, with the body softer and rounder.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-vend-sans: Contemporary and a little unusual, Origami's brush-lettered heading hands over to Vend Sans, whose ruler-straight line and tall x-height fill every row. Its wide, unclosed curve endings keep a long block of text moving smoothly.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-yaldevi: Brush-painted, blunt and heavy, Origami holds one line width around every curve. Yaldevi follows with an e opening clearly to the right and outsized lowercase, so a slightly larger body size would suit it.
gen-dafont-ostrich-sans-fs-erode: Erode has a tall middle band with shallow ascenders and a gentle ebb and flow of stroke weight, giving a dignified, editorial voice. And Ostrich Sans stands narrow and tight beside it, so the closed, vinyl-cut heading letters and the open, curving classic serif feel pleasantly opposed.
gen-dafont-ostrich-sans-fs-paquito: Tall, narrow lowercase with firmly pressed letters is what Ostrich Sans does best, with barely a sliver inside the c. But Paquito, a classic serif with almost no gap between x-height and caps, feels confident and approachable, so a longer passage in it reads more sturdily than that heading would.
gen-dafont-outrun-future-gf-abeezee: ABeeZee has terminals that finish well clear of the stem and a mean line set high, giving a friendly body. ABeeZee handles the steady reading, while Outrun Future, wide-spaced with a finger-traceable outline, handles the synthwave swagger.
gen-dafont-outrun-future-gf-aldrich: Aldrich has an x-height close to cap height and round letters that look cupped, like tracing one thick thread. Outrun Future makes the loud entrance; Aldrich does the steady work.
gen-dafont-outrun-future-gf-alexandria: Wide-set, outlined and unmistakably synthwave, Outrun Future leads, then Alexandria follows as a plain sans with open c terminals and a tall body. The heading makes the statement and the text quietly carries it.
